meta.note: TWO-STORY OPEN-FACED SCAFFOLD structure (the sim's street view is the elevation). Built from ScaffoldsSupply 5'W x 6'4"T walk-thru frames (1-11/16" dia tube, no center pins) with 7' x 4'-lock-span cross braces: each bay is 7ft wide x 5ft deep x 6'4" tall (2.13 x 1.52 x 1.93 m); adjacent rooms SHARE one frame, so bays abut with no gaps. floor 0 = ground, floor 1 = upper (+1.93m), 'both' = full-height climb rooms (up in Guy Line Climb, down in Vertical Moop March). Room names must match light_config.json, sensor names must match client/config-unit-*.json.
meta.sim_only: This file affects ONLY the simulator's 3D geometry. Lights/effects/audio/triggers all come from the production configs.
meta.enclosures: each room's "enclosure" is the wooden node box (XIAO C3 + sensor + power) from wiring-guides/room-node-enclosure-plan.md, hose-clamped to a scaffold frame member — and it holds ALL of the room's sensing. 12 rooms sense with an LD2410C mmWave radar, Cuddle Cross with an LD2450 tracker (sole radar since 2026-08-20 — presence + projection/orb tracks); Entrance and Exit sense with a TOF200C ToF module and are the only two boxes with an opening (940 nm won't pass ply; mmWave will). Wing bays: radar behind the ply window on the ENTRY-side front leg (ground enters west, upper enters east) at 1.55 m, boresight (yaw_deg, local +z) at the diagonally-opposite back corner, down-tilt 10° ground / 5° upper. Cuddle Cross: radar on the hex back corner aimed across the deck. Entrance/Exit: ToF fires from the box out through the START/FINISH arch (radar can't be used — it would see through the shared divider into the other half, and the foil fix was ruled out 2026-07-30). Guy Line/VMM: radar at the TOP of the room pointed straight down (fov 360 = the floor footprint it covers) so it sees someone at the bottom however they got there — through the doorway or down the ropes/scaffolding. Buttons and knock pads stay at their interaction points and 2-wire back to terminals in the room's box. Zone sensors in `sensors` carry pos (= the box), yaw_deg/tilt_deg/fov_deg/range_m and a room-bounds clip; `doorways` declares the arch openings the old doorway beams used to imply.

hex_center.note: The center is a hexagon of SIX complete 5'W x 6'4" walk-thru frames per level (12 total), hose-clamped in pairs at every corner — NO cross braces, no cut-down pieces. Side = 5ft (1.524m). A CORNER points at the street: the two angled street frames meeting at it are the split entry (START, east) and exit (FINISH, west) — each frame's walk-thru arch is one door, and the ground-floor Exit/Entrance divider runs front corner to back corner between them. The flat east/west frames' arches are the doorways the side rooms walk in through (the wings END at these flat frames — x=8.724 / x=11.364 — sharing them: one frame per junction, the wing bays’ cross braces pin directly to the hex frames); the two back frames are skinned. Upper deck = Cuddle Cross.

backgrounds.note: one wide printed canvas per level spans BOTH skinned back faces (west face = left half, east face = right half): the ground canvas backs the Exit and Entrance halves, the upper canvas backs Cuddle Cross

center_pole.note: a SINGLE continuous 20 ft stick of 3" schedule 40 pipe (3.5" OD) standing at the exact hex center: up from the ground where the Exit|Entrance divider meets the middle, through the Cuddle Cross deck and the hex roof, straight to the sky ~7 ft above the structure. One piece, no joints; the deck and roof penetrations are the lateral bracing.

beacon.note: THE BEACON: four tiki heads boxed square around the mast top, all four panel TOPS FLUSH with the pole tip at 6.096 m. Each face is a 24"x36" ply panel (1728x2592 @ 72 dpi in the art files) painted forest green, its line work laser-cut on the xTool from the REAL cut files cad-items/tiki-1..4.svg — the sim serves those same files at /cad/ so a cut-file edit shows up on the next reload. In each SVG the cls-1 rect is the painted panel and the single cls-2 path is what the laser cuts THROUGH; light from the LED-lit backing panel comes through the cuts, so the sim renders cls-1 as paint and makes cls-2 glow in the led color (LED hardware/color undecided — warm-white placeholder). Panels stand off half a panel width so their edges meet at the corners: a closed 24" square totem head the 3.5" pipe runs up the middle of. Face order marching around: tiki-1 street (+z), tiki-2 east/Entrance (+x), tiki-3 back (-z), tiki-4 west/Exit (-x). Delete this key to drop the beacon from the sim.

Guy Line Laser.note: LD2410C on the Guy Line Climb top of the room at 3.70 m pointed straight down; converted from ToF 2026-07-30 (Tim's placement). The ropes go in all directions and can't be arranged predictably, and people reach the bottom either through the doorway or by climbing down the ropes or the scaffolding — so the sensor has to cover the whole floor and see them at the bottom however they arrived. A doorway beam misses anyone coming down from above; any horizontal beam can be stood beside. fov 360 = the down-looking floor footprint (covers the shaft, clipped to the room), not a horizontal wedge.

projection.note: Cuddle Cross floor-projection rig: used ViewSonic LS625X (laser-phosphor DLP, 20k-hr solid-state source, SEALED optical engine + waveform dust filter - the playa-relevant feature; XGA 4:3, 3200 lm, TR 0.49:1, lens offset 118%, native focus 60-300in; ~$395 used on eBay 2026-07) mounted FACE-DOWN = NOSE-DOWN (0.22 m chassis depth hangs vertically; body top 3.82 kisses the 3.83 roof slab, so the window rides at ~1.53 m - the biggest image the roof allows: 3.112 m wide x 2.334 m along-throw) on a STUB ARM just INSIDE the hexagon's NE corner (paired legs at (11.364, 2.022); lens plumb 10 cm inboard of the vertex, body rear face ~1.5 cm off the leg cluster, arm_deg 60 out to the legs - the legs sit BEHIND the aperture so no scaffold steel touches a single ray), throwing SW down the long diagonal (yaw -120). 2026-07-18 MAX-COVERAGE revision - Tim's call: coverage math wins over the rear-leg placement preference. The geometry: with height roof-capped the image rect is fixed, so coverage is pure plumb+yaw placement; the 118% offset pins the near image edge 0.42 m from the lens plumb, and the far edge reaches only 2.754 m - short of the 3.048 m corner-to-corner diagonal - so some dark deck is unavoidable and the corner throw minimizes it. KEY OBSTRUCTION PHYSICS (caught by Tim): the ideal unobstructed plumb is ~6 cm OUTSIDE the vertex (92.7%, image dead-centered), but from there the paired corner legs stand 6 cm in front of the lens and every ray crosses them at 1.30-1.49 m height - one 43 mm tube at that range shadows a +-20 deg wedge through the FULL image depth, so any outboard aperture is optically dead; inboard-of-the-legs is the real optimum: 91.2% of the 6.03 m2 deck. All six corners tie; NE chosen because the S corner is blocked (canvas + node box in the near field), SE had the button rail in the beam (rail removed 2026-07-23 - the orb is the Cuddle control surface), SW rides the canvas end seam, and N hangs over the front lean-out corner. Unlit: the near corner wedge under the body (~0.52 m deep - the body hangs over the deck's darkest dead corner, bottom at 1.53 m) and the ~0.19 m SW far tip; the east-arch jamb clips only rays that land off-deck (masked). Fallbacks: rolling the body to yaw -63 at the OLD rear-leg clamp gets 89.8% with zero new hardware (the due-west throw was 75.8%; legs/arch clear there too); a roof-top doghouse over a beam porthole reaches 100% but means roof surgery. Offset tolerance now cuts both ways: 118%+-5% spans 88.2-92.6% (low-offset units win), so slot the arm bracket +-8 cm radially and set the final plumb on-site; every 25 mm of lost mount height costs ~0.4pt. MASKED to the deck outline as always (off-deck pixels black); mast base in-image (content island; its shadow wedge now falls SW toward the back-west corner, clear of the old button-station corner). Supersedes the rear-leg placement, the Casio XJ-ST145 pick (kept as budget fallback) and the earlier 595Wi scheme. LD2450/LD2410C node box unchanged at the back corner. Render Pi 3B outputs 1024x768. Playa care: ply shroud with open downward aperture, filter cloth over the intake, daily brush-out, power off by day. An LD2450 position radar joins the LD2410C inside the node box (UART1 on the XIAO C3) and streams up to 3 target positions to the projection Pi 3B at the rack; the sim reacts to the walker through the tracker's real coverage wedge with ~150 ms sensor+render latency. Show starts on the room's entry trigger (or tracked presence) and times out like the cue daemon. 2026-07-29 MOUNT DIMS for the arm/enclosure build: pos/h made mm-exact from the optics (window height above deck = TR 0.49 x 3.112 m image width = 1.525 m; pos = BODY-CENTER plumb, drawn lens window bd/2-0.03 = 27.5 mm ahead of it, which lands the lens plumb exactly 100 mm in from the NE deck corner ON the corner-to-corner string line) and the sim's Mount button overlays the calculated build position dimensioned off tape-measurable datums: lens plumb 100 mm from the corner along the string line, window 1525 mm above deck, body top 1745 mm (15 mm under the 1760 roof-slab soffit), rear face 15 mm off the leg pair, image near/far edges 520 / 2854 mm from the corner as deck verification marks. Fab spec + on-site calibration: wiring-guides/cuddle-projector-mount.md. 2026-07-29 STAND-OFF REVISION (Tim caught the body drawn through the frame bars): the walk-thru frames carry a TOP RAIL 75 mm below the leg tops and a full-width HEADER 190 mm down (the real PSV-610 members the sim frames model) - at the old 15 mm-off-the-legs position the body's rear corners overhung the frame planes ~60 mm straight through both bands, a REAL collision the 07-18 roof-cap math missed (it only checked the 3.83 roof slab; dropping under the header instead would gut the image - the 220 mm body can't thread the 77 mm rail-header gap). Fix: the whole rig slides 120 mm INBOARD down the throw diagonal - window height and image size unchanged, the mapping only translates: lens plumb now 220 mm from the corner, near/far image edges 640/2974 mm (far tip 74 mm shy - nearly closed), rear face 135 mm off the corner datum, rear corners 44 mm inside the worst-case frame plane = 25 mm clear of the rail tube even if the frames stand ON the deck edge. Coverage 91.2 -> 88.1% nominal; the fab-drawing leg ring stands ~3% (~40 mm) outside the idealized hex, so on-site the arm's +-80 mm slot slides the body back OUTBOARD to ~25 mm shy of the actual steel and recovers ~1-2 pt. Mount hardware now drawn for real: YOKE plate (280 mm tall, 3-ply lamination) hose-clamped to the paired corner legs in the two clean bands (~1540 above deck = below the brace studs, and ~1755 = above the top-rail weld under the coupling collar), box-BEAM arm threading the 77 mm rail-header gap at ~1658 above deck on the corner bisector (60 deg to each frame face) with a +-80 mm carriage slot, and the laser-cut ply SHROUD sleeve around the nose-down body (open bottom, top panel ~6 mm under the roof slab; cut files enclosure/projector-shroud.scad, export-shroud.py). 2026-08-01 REAL-DIMS + OFFSET CORRECTION (official LS625X user guide + datasheet pulled; Tim confirmed the model): (1) chassis corrected to the guide p.56 figures - 383.7 w x 291.5 d x 147.7 h mm, net 6.2 kg, 305 W normal, ceiling bosses 4x M4 on 223.0 x 150.0 - the 07-18 body (293 x 221.5 x 114.6) was a bad source, ~0.76x in every axis; (2) the offset convention was misread - the guide p.13 throw table puts the image near edge 8.95% of image height from the lens axis (118% means center over HALF-height), while the July math used 18% of full height, double the truth. Consequences, all applied here: the 291.5 mm nose-down body no longer fits under the 1760 soffit at window 1525 -> window drops to 1455 mm (soffit 1760 - 6 service - 2.9 top - 4.5 headroom - 291.5 body), image 2969 x 2227 mm (TR 0.49), lens plumb 250 mm from the corner (shroud rear corners 25 mm clear of the rail tube worst-case, same standard as 07-29), near/far deck marks 449/2676 (far tip 372 shy), image center 1563 from the corner, lit coverage 90.2% nominal - BETTER than the misread 88.1% because the corrected offset re-centers the smaller image. pos = body-center plumb = lens plumb (lens assumed CENTERED along-throw on the 147.7 face - MEASURE from the unit; its lateral off-center in the 383.7 width is handled at the bench: drill the carriage plate so the LENS, not the chassis, lands on the string line). Carriage re-sized for the real boss pattern (PI-shaped plate 260 x 240 around the beam, 4x M4x16 with washers), beam adjustment slots re-centered on the carriage bolt line (the 07-29 sheet had them at the far inboard end where the carriage never rides - latent, never built), shroud cavity 391.7 x 156.1 x 296, side vents 90 x 160. Cut files re-exported; fab spec rewritten. Delete this key to remove the whole rig from the sim.

eye.note: Cuddle orb (sim preview only, no production config): a Waveshare ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-1.28 round display (chip verified 2026-07-22: ESP32-S3R8, 16MB flash, 8MB PSRAM, native USB-Serial-JTAG, MAC fc:01:2c:d1:e2:3c) at the REAR of the room, tucked directly UNDER the back-corner sensor/node box (Tim 2026-07-23; supersedes both the mast idea - display inside the 3.5in pole - and the high-on-canvas spot). Same plumb as the LD2450 it reads. Renders a watching eye whose pupil tracks whoever the SAME node-box LD2450 the projection reads reports, with first-order lag. skin = hal (2001 red camera lens) or mayan (jade+gold jaguar/serpent deity eye, obsidian vertical slit); the sim's Eye button cycles off/hal/mayan. Real panel is 32.5mm (1.28"); diameter here is enlarged so the eye reads across the deck. The gestures the real orb sends hit the REST API directly (shake -> /api/run_effect_all_rooms LightningStorm, touch-wheel -> /api/set_theme next_theme, dock -> /api/stop_effect) - see wiring-guides/cuddle-orb-plan.md; they are NOT room-node sensors so they stay out of triggers.json. Delete this key to drop the orb from the sim.
